summary: sextant-cli-linux-arm64 ships an opaque WebRTC P2P remote-control agent binary
details: The package contains a single 12MB linux/arm64 Go ELF at bin/sxt (sha256 5e07576f95d37b6ee865e559f25362862d5d3c8d5725cced0f9ca197e79b5d34) with no README, no source, no signature, and no scripts or main entry. The binary statically links the canonical stack for a NAT-traversing peer-to-peer remote-control agent: pion/webrtc/v4, pion/turn/v5, pion/ice/v4, pion/dtls/v3, pion/sctp, pion/datachannel, coder/websocket, and skip2/go-qrcode (QR-code operator pairing). package.json declares the package name as `sextant-cli-linux-arm64` but its license field points at an unrelated repository, `https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control`, whose account and repo names describe remote-control functionality rather than a `sextant` project. The WebRTC + STUN/TURN + datachannel + QR-pairing composition provides a remote operator with an interactive, NAT-piercing control channel to the host on which the binary is executed, and the provenance mismatch between the package name and the referenced `claude_control` repo is consistent with a covert remote agent distributed as a platform-scoped optional dependency of a parent `sextant-cli` package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
